Evaluate a feature-grouping tool against the MS1Match reference set

evaluate_grouping.Rd

For each library compound, the Tier 1a [M+H]+ feature is the anchor and the group the tool assigns to it defines the compound's expected group. Each reference feature (Phase 1 and Phase 2) gets the first status that applies: Ref-unassigned (no-anchor) if the tool did not group the anchor, Ref-unassigned if the anchor is grouped but the feature is not, otherwise Ref-confirmed or Ref-conflicting. Every other feature of the tool is Ref-unmatched, co-grouped (in a group with a compound anchor) or Ref-unmatched, unrelated (in a group without an anchor, or in no group).

Usage

evaluate_grouping(
  anno_result,
  grouping,
  tool_name = "tool",
  rt_window = NULL,
  feature_table,
  mz_tol = 0.001,
  rt_tol = 1
)

Arguments

anno_result

Output of join_annotation_results(). Uses export_feature_compound_summary (reference rows) and export_reduced_anno_table (anchor search).

grouping

Output of prepare_grouping_table, camera_to_grouping or ramclustr_to_grouping.

tool_name

Label used in printed output and in compare_grouping.

rt_window

Optional c(min, max) in seconds. Applied only to features outside the reference set (Ref-unmatched), so their counts are comparable between tools.

feature_table

The feature table MS1Match was run on. The function stops unless check_feature_match confirms that the grouping and MS1Match used the same table. If one is a subset of the other, only features present in both are evaluated.

mz_tol, rt_tol

Passed to check_feature_match.

Value

Object of class grouping_evaluation: a list with tool, benchmark (tier table; pct_grouped is the share of reference features the tool grouped at all, i.e. its coverage), status_counts, full_table (one row per reference feature x compound, plus one per feature outside the reference set), anchors and feature_match.

Details

The grouping table must list every feature the tool processed, including those it did not group (group = NA). A feature missing from the grouping table is treated as outside the shared feature table and excluded, not counted as Ref-unassigned.
